title: Language
description: The language module displays the currently selected language.

format.label: What to show
format.doc: The format, how information should be displayed.
format.description: The text shown in the bar. Words in curly braces, like {icon}, are replaced with live values: see the list of placeholders.

keyboard-name.label: Keyboard name
keyboard-name.doc: Specifies which keyboard to use from hyprctl devices output. Using the option that begins with "at-translated-set..." is recommended.
keyboard-name.description: Specifies which keyboard to use from hyprctl devices output. Using the option that begins with "at-translated-set..." is recommended.

menu.label: Open popup menu with
menu.description: Which click opens a popup menu for this module.

menu-file.label: Menu layout file
menu-file.doc: Location of the menu descriptor file. There need to be an element of type GtkMenu with id menu
menu-file.description: The file that describes the menu entries (a GTK .xml file with a menu called "menu").

menu-actions.label: Menu commands
menu-actions.doc: The actions corresponding to the buttons of the menu.
menu-actions.description: For each menu entry, the command to run when you pick it.

tooltip.label: Show tooltip
tooltip.doc: Enables or disables the tooltip for the language module. By default, the tooltip is enabled. Set to false to disable.
tooltip.description: Show a small popup with more details when the mouse is over the module.

tooltip-format.label: Tooltip text
tooltip-format.doc: Specifies the format of the tooltip when it is enabled. It follows the same format replacement rules as the format key.
tooltip-format.description: What the popup shows. It uses the same placeholders as the bar text.

expand.label: Fill empty space
expand.doc: Enables this module to consume all left over space dynamically.
expand.description: Stretch the module to use all the free space left in its section.

patterns.label: Format <lang>
patterns.description: Provide an alternative name to display per language where <lang> is the language of your choosing. Can be passed multiple times with multiple languages as shown by the example below.

patterns.label: Format <lang> <variant>
patterns.description: Like format-<lang> but also matches the layout variant, taking precedence over format-<lang> when both the language and variant match.

patterns.label: Tooltip format <lang>
patterns.description: Allows specifying a different tooltip format for each language. The <lang> should be replaced with the language code. This can be used to provide a custom tooltip for each language.

patterns.label: Tooltip format <lang> <variant>
patterns.description: Like tooltip-format-<lang> but also matches the layout variant, taking precedence over tooltip-format-<lang> when both the language and variant match.
